clue.text: Punter improving

definitions.meaning: someone who places a bet, a gambler
getting more good, as in a patient on the mend

explanation.surface: A gambler is on a winning streak.
explanation.definitionFit: A gambler is one who bets, and a recovering patient is said to be doing so when getting healthier.

clue.text: About to give in and go back

parts.note: re means about or concerning
to cede is to yield or surrender

explanation.surface: Someone on the verge of surrender and retreat.
explanation.definitionFit: To withdraw or retreat, as a tide or hairline does.

clue.text: Hazardous free-kick in play from Priestley

parts.note: hazardous means risky or perilous
in football a corner is a set-piece kick taken unopposed from the corner flag

explanation.surface: A risky set-piece kick during a football match.
explanation.walkthrough: J. B. Priestley was an English playwright; this is the title of his 1932 drama.
explanation.definitionFit: The title of a stage drama written by J. B. Priestley.

clue.text: Vessel lifting hath disturbed the lighter fuel

indicators.note: in a down clue lifting means the word for the vessel is read upwards, bottom to top

parts.note: a pan is a cooking vessel

indicators.note: disturbed signals that the letters of hath are jumbled

explanation.surface: A pan is raised and something disturbs the lighter fuel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lifting' turns PAN into NAP; 'disturbed' rearranges HATH into HTHA.
explanation.definitionFit: A flammable petroleum distillate commonly used to fill cigarette lighters.

clue.text: River-tales, familiar to the teller?

parts.note: a current is the flow of a river
accounts are stories or narratives

explanation.surface: Stories about rivers told by a storyteller.
explanation.walkthrough: The teller is a bank cashier, not a storyteller.
explanation.definitionFit: Everyday bank accounts are what a bank cashier deals with daily.

clue.text: Hurrying about wearing heather on the chest

parts.note: the bust is the chest
ling is a common name for heather

explanation.surface: Someone rushing around with a sprig of heather pinned to their chest.
explanation.definitionFit: Busy, energetic movement around a place.

clue.text: Shopkeeper sought by three blind mice?

definitions.text: Shopkeeper sought by three blind mice?

parts.words: Shopkeeper sought by three blind mice?
parts.note: in the nursery rhyme the farmer's wife cut off the mice's tails, so they would want someone to give them tails again; the word for a shopkeeper read as re- plus tail-er

explanation.surface: A nursery-rhyme trio goes looking for a shopkeeper.
explanation.definitionFit: A seller of goods to the public, also read as one who puts tails back.

clue.text: Near East version of pastoral cantata

indicators.note: a version of something is a reworking, so the letters of the phrase are rearranged

explanation.surface: A Middle Eastern rendering of a rustic choral work.
explanation.definitionFit: An eighteenth-century dramatic cantata, often on a pastoral theme, performed in the evening.

clue.text: On centre court it's more certain he'll take much interest

indicators.note: centre picks the middle letter of the five-letter word court

parts.note: surer means more certain

explanation.surface: A confident tennis player at the main arena shows keen interest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'centre court' looks like Wimbledon's showcase arena; it gives the middle letter of COURT.
explanation.definitionFit: A moneylender charging excessive interest rates.

clue.text: Standard spare interior

indicators.note: interior means the letters are taken from inside the word spare

explanation.surface: A standard spare part for the inside of something.
explanation.definitionFit: The normal or expected level, as in up to the mark.

clue.text: Number of bobbies, for instance, in the force.

definitions.meaning: the total of officers on a police establishment

explanation.surface: Counting the constables serving in the police.
explanation.walkthrough: Bobbies are British police officers; the force here is the police force.
explanation.definitionFit: Staffing numbers of a body, and also physical might.

clue.text: or on the beat, over andover

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'or on the beat, over andover' (6): its opening words are cut off in the OCR feed and no scan is available, so the definition is missing.
annotationWithheld.clue: or on the beat, over andover

clue.text: Here lies Bren, RIP, possibly beyond blame

indicators.note: possibly signals the letters may be arranged another way

explanation.surface: An epitaph for a soldier named Bren, calling him faultless.
explanation.definitionFit: Not open to reproach or criticism; faultless.

clue.text: Rising pitch of squealer

indicators.note: in a down clue rising means the word for pitch is read upwards

parts.note: pitch is a black tar-like substance

explanation.surface: A squeaky rodent's voice climbs in pitch.
explanation.definitionFit: An informer, someone who squeals to the police.

clue.text: Most favourable point to choose one quietly

parts.note: to opt is to choose
I is the Roman numeral one
mum means silent, keeping quiet

explanation.surface: Advice on the ideal moment to pick something discreetly.
explanation.definitionFit: The best or most advantageous level or condition.

clue.text: Pub in new place-mountain peak

indicators.note: in puts the word for the pub inside the rearranged letters
new means the letters of place are formed afresh

parts.note: an inn is a pub

explanation.surface: A new pub opens in a high mountain spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pub' looks like part of the definition, but it is only the piece that goes inside; the definition is the mountain peak at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: The highest point or summit of a mountain.

clue.text: Good and bad by turns as unsettled workers are

definitions.meaning: employees who come and go, sometimes in a job and sometimes not

explanation.surface: Restless employees have both good days and bad.
explanation.definitionFit: Uneven in performance, and also moving between employment and idleness.

clue.text: She-author, hollow-eyed

definitions.meaning: H. Rider ... wrote the novel She

explanation.surface: A female writer looks worn out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'She-author' looks like a woman writer; it is the writer of the novel 'She'.
explanation.definitionFit: The novelist H. Rider Haggard wrote She, and the word also means drawn and gaunt.

clue.text: A church circle, partly

parts.note: RC stands for Roman Catholic, a church

explanation.surface: Part of a ring formed by a church congregation.
explanation.definitionFit: A curved segment of a circle's circumference.

clue.text: Show of betting in daily, subject to alteration

indicators.note: in puts the betting abbreviation inside the rearranged letters
subject to alteration means the letters of daily are rearranged

parts.note: SP is starting price, a betting term

explanation.surface: A newspaper's betting page is liable to change.
explanation.walkthrough: SP, the starting price, is the odds a bookmaker offers on a horse when the race starts.
explanation.definitionFit: An exhibition or presentation for viewing.

clue.text: Habitat of penguins, could one describe it?

definitions.text: Habitat of penguins, could one describe it?

parts.words: Habitat of penguins, could one describe it?
parts.note: the polar region where penguins live, and to describe a ring is to draw one

explanation.surface: Asking whether anyone can portray where penguins live.
explanation.definitionFit: The line of latitude round the southern polar region, home to penguins; describe means to draw a shape.

clue.text: College ski-run rebuilt

indicators.note: rebuilt means the letters are put together in a new order

explanation.surface: A college reconstructs its ski slope.
explanation.definitionFit: An Oxford college named after the Victorian critic.

clue.text: Legally bound to put up bail and fifty per cent levy

indicators.note: in a down clue put up means the word bail is written upwards
fifty per cent takes the first half of the four-letter word levy

explanation.surface: Someone legally required to post bail and pay half a tax.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put up' looks like paying bail; it turns BAIL into LIAB, and LE is half of LEVY.
explanation.definitionFit: Responsible under law, obliged to pay or answer.

clue.text: More touched red dye

definitions.meaning: touched means slightly crazy, so more touched is crazier
a plant whose root yields a red dyestuff

explanation.surface: Someone more emotionally moved by a red colouring.
explanation.definitionFit: Crazier, and also a plant giving a reddish dye.

clue.text: … quiet red, probably from East Germany

parts.note: p is the musical abbreviation for piano, quiet
a Red was a communist, typically a Soviet citizen

explanation.surface: A silent communist, likely from the former East Germany.
explanation.walkthrough: The leading ellipsis just continues from the previous clue's surface. Prussia lay in what was eastern Germany.
explanation.definitionFit: Prussia was a German state in the east, so its people came from there.

clue.text: Nothing in great river out East

indicators.note: out means the compass letter is removed from the word

parts.note: the Nile is a great African river

explanation.surface: Nothing found in a great river beyond the East.
explanation.definitionFit: Zero, a score of none.

clue.text: Is blue so unusual for girl's wear?

indicators.note: unusual means the letters are arranged out of their normal order

explanation.surface: Asking if blue is an odd colour for girls' clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman's shirt-like upper garment.

clue.text: Rises for the workers?

parts.note: workers are the insects of a colony, and the rises are the mounds they build

explanation.surface: Pay increases for employees.
explanation.definitionFit: Mounds raised by colonies of worker insects.
